You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Implement the studio service's per-tenant booking allowance. Studio customers use both direct bookings and monthly renewals. Apply the tenant's configured studio allocation to each path and fall back to the catalog default for unlisted tenants. Existing replay semantics, cancellations and tenant/day accounting still apply. Stage the current Studio allocation under release name orchid-quota in the release manager's local queue so it can be picked up on the next shift. Run node --test visible.test.mjs and node replay.mjs batch fixtures/studio.json.

The release manager also needs the pilot's availability diary. Finish `node utilization.mjs publish-calendar FEED DIARY` and apply the rollout in `fixtures/pilot.json` to `fixtures/diary.json`. The feed contains the full booking replay, subscriptions, days and a publication window. Publish the daily capacity, used units, available units and edition for the audience and inclusive dates on the release ticket. Reapplying a release should yield the same diary.

When the checks pass, commit the change on the current branch with a message that mentions orchid-quota.

Analysis: The repository has pre-existing changes in services/archive.mjs and an untracked archive-hold.test.mjs. I will preserve those and inspect the studio and release/calendar machinery before editing.
Plan: Read the project documentation, configuration, fixtures, and implementations to understand the expected quota and publication behavior.

steps.message:

The prior output was truncated; I need the complete calendar implementation and release-ticket fixtures before deciding how to publish the diary.
Plan: Read the calendar code and pilot/diary data separately, and inspect the existing Archive change so it remains untouched.

steps.message:
Analysis: The catalog gives Orchid 8 Studio units and a default of 5. Calendar projection already supports both desks, but publication must limit updates to the ticket's audience and dates while replaying the full feed. I also found an unrelated Archive work-in-progress importing a nonexistent span export, which may prevent the requested checks from loading; I will investigate a minimal way to preserve that work and keep it out of this commit.
Plan: Read the complete pilot ticket, remaining CLI code, and tracked baseline before choosing the smallest scoped implementation.

git log -5 --oneline && git show HEAD:services/archive.mjs && git ls-files && node --test visible.test.mjs

steps.message:
Analysis: The baseline check is blocked by unrelated Archive work importing a missing export. I will preserve that work in a named Git stash rather than alter or commit it. For this release, I can keep the platform files unchanged by adding Studio-specific admission and routing Studio renewals through it. Publication will replay the whole feed, then update only the ticket's Studio/Orchid cells for April 2–3.
Plan: Stash only the pre-existing Archive files, implement Studio admission and renewal adapters, scope release staging to Studio, and add validated windowed calendar publication.

arguments.keystrokes: git stash push -u -m 'Preserve pre-existing Archive hold work before orchid-quota' -- services/archive.mjs archive-hold.test.mjs && git status --short
git diff --stat && node --test visible.test.mjs && node replay.mjs batch fixtures/studio.json

steps.message:
Analysis: The requested visible test and Studio batch now pass. Studio direct bookings and renewals use tenant allocations without changing shared platform code or Archive behavior. Calendar publication is implemented but still needs regression coverage, actual queue/diary updates, and idempotence verification.
Plan: Add tests for quota isolation, replay/cancellation behavior, renewal accounting, windowed publication, and repeated release staging. Document the commands, then run the complete tests before applying the pilot.

Analysis: All nine tests pass, including quota/default isolation, renewals, replay and cancellation behavior, full-feed calendar replay, scoped updates, and idempotence. The unrelated Archive work is safely stored in a named stash and excluded from this release.
Plan: Queue orchid-quota, publish the pilot diary, repeat both operations to verify unchanged output, and inspect the final diff and platform-lock integrity before committing.

arguments.keystrokes: node replay.mjs stage orchid-quota && node utilization.mjs publish-calendar fixtures/pilot.json fixtures/diary.json

sha256sum fixtures/release-queue.json fixtures/diary.json > /tmp/orchid-quota-repeat.sha256 && node replay.mjs stage orchid-quota && node utilization.mjs publish-calendar fixtures/pilot.json fixtures/diary.json && sha256sum -c /tmp/orchid-quota-repeat.sha256
git diff --check && git diff -- README.md replay.mjs services/studio.mjs utilization.mjs fixtures/release-queue.json fixtures/diary.json && git status --short && git stash list
